entry.why: The packet establishes adult eligibility, elevated cardiovascular risk, a double-blind randomized design, and EPA/DHA treatment versus corn oil intended as an inert comparator. This meets the packet's question; established cardiovascular disease in every participant is not required.

quotes.span: ELIGIBILITY: Inclusion Criteria: 1. Men or women, ≥18 years of age.

To determine the effects on cardiovascular outcomes of a carboxylic acid formulation of EPA and DHA (omega-3 CA) with documented favorable effects on lipid and inflammatory markers in patients with atherogenic dyslipidemia and high cardiovascular risk.

A double-blind, randomized, multicenter trial (enrollment October 30, 2014, to June 14, 2017; study termination January 8, 2020; last patient visit May 14, 2020) comparing omega-3 CA with corn oil in statin-treated participants with high cardiovascular risk, hypertriglyceridemia, and low levels of high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C).

Participants were randomized to receive 4 g/d of omega-3 CA (n = 6539) or corn oil, which was intended to serve as an inert comparator (n = 6539), in addition to usual background therapies, including statins.
